title: Mobile App Engineering
tagline: Cross-platform mobile apps, native device APIs, offline synchronization, and release engineering
description: From mobile UI composition in React Native / Flutter to native bridge architecture, background tasks, local SQLite/WatermelonDB offline-first sync, and App Store automation.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of mobile user interaction

stages.title: Stage 1: Mobile UI & Navigation Paradigms
stages.description: Mobile lifecycle, safe areas, touch gesture responders, and native stack navigation.

nodes.title: Native Navigation & Screen Stacks
nodes.description: Deep linking, tab bars, modal presentations, and hardware back button handling.
nodes.whyItMatters: Web-style URL navigation feels sluggish on mobile if not backed by native OS screen primitives (UINavigationController, Android FragmentManager).
keyTakeaways: Always wrap screens in SafeAreaView to prevent notch and home-indicator overlap.
Support universal deep links (Apple Universal Links, Android App Links) for seamless onboarding.
Unmount heavy hidden screens or preserve state using memory-efficient stack configurations.
nodes.interviewTips: Expect questions on handling state during backgrounding and memory eviction by the mobile OS.

stages.title: Stage 2: Offline-First Architecture & Sync
stages.description: Local databases (SQLite, Realm), conflict resolution (CRDTs), and optimistic background sync.

nodes.title: Offline-First Data Sync with Local SQLite
nodes.description: Caching mutations locally in an offline queue, optimistic UI updates, and synchronization when connectivity is restored.
nodes.whyItMatters: Mobile users frequently lose network connectivity (subways, elevators, rural areas). An offline-first app remains completely functional and responsive.

resources.title: WatermelonDB: High Performance React Native Database

keyTakeaways: Write changes to local SQLite first, update UI optimistically, and enqueue a sync mutation job.
Implement deterministic conflict resolution strategies (e.g., Last-Write-Wins with timestamps or CRDTs).
Monitor network status using NetInfo and trigger background sync tasks when online.
nodes.interviewTips: Interviewers will ask how you handle clock skew across devices in offline sync conflict resolution.
